title: remove_on_error must re-raise the original error when partial-download cleanup fails
answers: artifact download shows PermissionError instead of the real download failure
partial file cleanup error hides the root cause of a failed download
why does download_artifacts report Permission denied on the destination file
remove_on_error swallows the original exception when os.remove fails
body:
Symptom: A failed artifact download reports a cleanup error (e.g. Permission denied on the partial file) instead of the real failure, such as chunks exhausting retries.
Root cause: mlflow/utils/file_utils.py:remove_on_error ran os.remove / shutil.rmtree unguarded in its except block, so a cleanup exception replaced the original and the trailing bare raise never ran.
Fix pattern: Wrap the cleanup call in its own try/except Exception, log the cleanup failure as a warning, and let the original exception propagate with a bare raise (same object, traceback intact).
Constraints: Cleanup inside an except block must never be allowed to raise over the caller's error. Applies to all callers of remove_on_error (multipart/cloud/databricks artifact downloads, _create_virtualenv).
applies: Any change to remove_on_error or to cleanup code run inside an except block that re-raises.
says: Artifact download failure screen shows permission denied instead of the network error.
Failed downloads mask the root cause with temporary file deletion errors.
Show why the model download failed rather than reporting cleanup permission issues.
Download error popup displays cleanup failure instead of retry exhaustion.
search: Cleanup handlers in mlflow/utils/file_utils.py:remove_on_error must wrap cleanup calls like os.remove and shutil.rmtree in try/except Exception to log cleanup failures as warnings and re-raise the original exception. Cleanup exceptions must never mask the caller's failure, such as retry exhaustion in multipart, cloud, or Databricks artifact downloads, or _create_virtualenv. Applies to changes to remove_on_error or any cleanup routine executing within an except block that re-raises.
